submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad first-token-sink head: at rest it attends to position 0 with strength near the floor (~0), and it spikes when it diverts to self-attend a mid-context content word or attend to the immediately previous content token. Spikes are strongest on the head noun of a sentence-initial noun phrase (controversy, differences, doors, pressure) and on the word right after such a noun, plus single-letter name initials; ordinary sentences are mixed (many rest, some cross weakly ~0.6-1.2), while single-word greetings and runs of repeated identical tokens stay at the sink inactive.

rival_explanations: Narrower event-noun detector: it fires only on abstract event/outcome nouns, so concrete-subject sentences like The dog lay on the rug and Please close the door quietly will test inactive.
Pure length/position detector: strength grows only with token count, so any long sentence will test active and any short one inactive regardless of wording.
